provider.architecture: Optional synchronous resolver/read/seeker callback table copied into each RexxVM; no kernel-global stream table and no filesystem calls.
provider.identity: Opaque borrowed identity returned only by the provider resolver; omitted name is a separate default-stream request, while an explicit empty name is a named lookup.
provider.cursor_owner: Provider owns and advances the cursor once by the returned byte count. The VM requests seek/read but never applies a second position update.
provider.lifetime: Embedding owns callback code, user_data, identities, and resources. It keeps user_data alive while installed; provider replacement is rejected during VM execution/callbacks. VM teardown does not release provider resources.
provider.sharing: Internal routines and INTERPRET share the VM provider and cursor. Independent VMs use independent contexts unless the embedding intentionally shares one.
provider.bounds: Length-bearing raw bytes; explicit result length; 16 MiB maximum; exact provider byte count; nonzero spans require borrowed non-null data. No strlen on stream data.
provider.production: No kernel provider is installed. Missing default or named access fails closed. Arbitrary paths, devices, and network endpoints are never opened.

compatibility_profile.selected: IBM z/OS 2.5 byte-oriented CHARIN contract, adapted to registered embedded identities.
compatibility_profile.arguments: CHARIN accepts zero through three arguments. Omitted name selects provider default; omitted start uses provider cursor; omitted length is 1. Start is an exact positive whole number from 1 through 4,294,967,295. Length is an exact whole number from 0 through 16 MiB. Explicit empty name remains distinct from omission. Extra, negative, fractional, nonnumeric, and zero-start values are rejected; oversized supported integers return resource-limit status.
compatibility_profile.sequential_and_seek: A successful read returns exactly the bytes supplied and provider cursor advances once by the actual count. Explicit one-based starts require a seekable identity. A zero-length call skips read; explicit start still seeks.
compatibility_profile.eof_short_reads: Positive short reads return all supplied bytes. EOF before bytes, unavailable input, provider errors, unsupported operations, and malformed metadata retain distinct VM statuses. No read blocks or polls.
compatibility_profile.condition_gap: Byte-stream statuses enter the existing generic SYNTAX condition with description 'Stream I/O error'. RX33 does not retain a per-stream error flag or expose STREAM/NOTREADY state. A successful short read does not set a queryable IBM-style stream error, so CHARIN remains Partial.

covered: Resolution unavailable, unknown identity, callback error, and invalid metadata.
Read EOF, unavailable, provider error, pending, unsupported, zero-byte EOF, malformed pointer/length/ownership/EOF metadata, and successful short read.
Seek unsupported and provider error, including zero-length seek without reading.
Allocation failure before provider resolution/read leaves the cursor unchanged.
Test-only borrowed-buffer copy refusal after provider read clears the result and advances exactly once, as defined by provider-owned cursor policy.
Provider replacement and VM teardown attempted during callbacks are rejected safely.
Separate provider contexts in multiple VMs, VM teardown cycles, and recovery after catchable stream errors.

remaining_limits: No retained per-stream EOF/NOTREADY error state and no STREAM built-in query path.
No approved production default or named byte-stream provider in the kernel.
No positive native stream read; native qualification covers fail-closed behavior and recovery only.
Provider callbacks must return synchronously; pending and blocking behavior is unsupported.
Raw byte semantics do not transcode EBCDIC, DBCS, Unicode, or locale encodings.
CHAROUT, LINEIN, LINEOUT, CHARS, LINES, STREAM, filesystem mounting, and interactive Console input remain out of scope.
The RX20 native guest capture showed TIME(E) progression but did not show TIME(R) progression or RX20_NATIVE_CLOCK_CAPABILITY_DONE; per-command REXX exit status was not captured.
